html:
The first women's rights convention in the United States, held over two days in July 1848 in a chapel in Seneca Falls, New York. It launched the long campaign for women's right to vote.

The main organisers were Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott. The two had met in 1840 at an anti-slavery conference in London, where women delegates were not allowed to take part.

About 300 people attended. They debated a Declaration of Sentiments that Stanton had modelled on the Declaration of Independence: "all men and women are created equal". It listed the wrongs done to women in law, property, work, education and the church. One hundred people signed it, 68 women and 32 men.

The demand for the vote was the most controversial point, and many thought it went too far. It passed after Frederick Douglass spoke for it. American women finally won the vote with the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920, 72 years later.
sum: The first women's rights convention in the United States, held over two days in July 1848 in a chapel in Seneca Falls, New York. It launched the long campaign for women's right to vote.
